title: [Model Loader] Run model-level post-load finalization from the loader hook
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**`load_weights` must not assume all weights arrive in one call.** RL weight updates call it once per bucket: verl sends 512 MB buckets tensor by tensor, and the NCCL engine calls it once per tensor (inside `disable_mtp_completeness_check()`). So a weight and its scale, or the two halves of a merged tensor, can land in different calls. Any post-load work inside `load_weights` then runs on partial weights, once per bucket. Context: RFC #54477, tracker #50079.

The PR has three parts:
1. **One finish step for every load.** `finalize_model_weights(model)` runs once after a full load and once at the end of every reload, and calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. There are no per-model opt-ins. This mirrors SGLang, which post-processes once at `end_weight_update`.
2. **Split merged tensors written through the weight loader.** Molmo/Molmo2 embedding halves and Llama4 DP-vision q/k/v are written straight into their rows, so any split or order of calls works. Nothing is parked across calls.
3. **Post-load work moves out of `load_weights` into the hook.** That includes the blocks that used to rebuild derived state on every call.

Coverage: an AST script enumerated every `def load_weights` in `vllm/` (447), and each was checked in source. That covers multimodal wrappers, MTP/EAGLE/DSpark/DFlash drafters, adapters, `AutoWeightsLoader`, layer-level loaders, model loaders and the `vllm/models/*` platform variants. Every model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` was also checked for whether it is safe to re-run on new weights.

## Claims

**Finish step.** `finalize_model_weights` is called from two places, and nowhere else:
- `model_loader/utils.py::process_weights_after_loading`: cold load (dummy loads too), after per-layer quant processing.
- `finalize_layerwise_reload`: used by `reload_weights` and by `finish_weight_update` in the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.

No `load_weights` calls the model hook anymore. Code that restores layers in the middle of a load (the torchao reload decorator and the expert-substitution error path) calls `finalize_layerwise_processing` and leaves the model hook to the finish step. The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop `finalizes_weights_during_load`, `_weights_finalized` and the regrouping that loaded the language model first, and `stream_language_model_first` is deleted.

**Split merged tensors.** Each part is written into its rows of the target parameter by a weight loader, in any order and across calls:
- **Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding:** `wte.embedding` and `wte.new_embedding` go into their rows of this rank's `embed_tokens` vocab shard (`_load_split_embedding`). Before, a call without both halves raised `KeyError`.
- **Llama4 DP-vision q/k/v:** the replicated `qkv_proj` gets a shard loader (`_load_qkv_shard`), so q/k/v go through the stacked mapping; `_consolidate_qkv_weights` is removed. Before, a split triple failed in `torch.cat`.

**Same as main (follow-up on #58382).** These combine several checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights` and keep main's handling here: FP8 indexer `wk` dequant (DeepSeek-V2, `deepseek_mtp`, DeepSeek-V3.2, HY-V4, dots3, GLM5-next), GLM5-next FP8 MLA projections, MiMo-V2/MTP fused FP8 qkv, and the Jina-v3 LoRA merge. They move to checkpoint-layout parameters combined in `process_weights_after_loading`, on top of #58382 (PR 6 in the [RFC tracker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477#issuecomment-6450991360)). Until then a weight and its scale split across calls behave as on main.

**Moved from `load_weights` to `process_weights_after_loading`:**
- **DFlash-family fused context-KV buffers:** Qwen3 DFlash, plus Qwen3 DSpark, Gemma4 DSpark and LiLiCorr through the inherited hook, and Laguna.
  - The hook now runs after quant processing, so it reads processed weights.
  - The fused path that reads raw weights is used only when the projections are unquantized and not repacked by CPU (`_reads_raw_weights`).
  - Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method, as Qwen3 DFlash already did for quantized drafts.
  - On a reload the rebuilt buffers are copied into the existing ones (`_rebuild_in_place`). Model Runner V2 records the context-KV step in its FULL CUDA graph, so a new allocation would leave the graph reading the old weights. LiLiCorr's inference buffers, used inside the DFlash2 graph, go through the same helper.
- **BERT MLM:** the tied-decoder copy, decided by `config.tie_word_embeddings`.
- **DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA and V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD:** the mHC broadcast.
- **LiLiCorr:** the inference buffers. A `dummy` load now builds them.
- **OpenPangu:** the `post_weight_load` sweep. `StaticSinkAttention.update_sink_kv` now clears `sink_populated`, so a re-run rewrites the cached sink KV.
- **Gemma4 MTP:** the lm-head cache invalidation and the suppress-token index.
- **DeepSeek-V4 XPU:** `finalize_mega_moe_weights` for target, MTP and DSpark. The guarded lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` stays for dummy loads.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA:** the Engram page-cache drop and THP collapse.
- **dots3 vision:** the hook runs at every reload finish, so the block compile is done only once.

**Decisions on one call's loaded set run only for a complete load.** They are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`, which the weight-transfer engines turn off. They used to fire on every bucket:
- `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- DSpark `confidence_head` drops: gemma4, qwen3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1.
- Checkpoint checks: Qwen3 DSpark, Eagle3 `mask_hidden`, AliceAI and LiLiCorr coverage.
- The NemotronVL seq-cls head init.
- The MTP layer checks that were still ungated: Bailing V3, DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next, Kimi-K3.
- **The Phi-3-V embedding tie.**
  - After the cold-load tie, `embed_tokens.weight` became the canonical name of the shared embedding.
  - So the checkpoint's `model.embed_tokens.weight` was skipped as its alias, and every reload either raised (main) or left the embedding stale.
  - The tie now re-registers `embed_tokens` last, so the language model's name stays canonical and reloads write it.

## Validation

GB300, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8e2beaa3bf…` with each tree's `vllm/**/*.py` overlaid. The two arms:
- **main** is `817fa3518c`.
- **PR** is `2152968d0f`, plus `361a9a4c11` rerun on every case it touches.

Both arms always ran on the same GPU type.

**E1, cold start: no change.**
- The full state fingerprint is identical on main and PR for 18 models. It covers every param and buffer, plus the tensors and numbers reachable from module attributes (for example DSv4 mHC, DFlash fused KV, BERT tie and MiMo FP8 qkv).
- Greedy outputs are identical wherever main matches itself across two runs.
- GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) is within main's own run-to-run noise:

| model | GSM8K main / PR | spec accept rate main / PR |
|---|---|---|
| Phi-3-vision-128k-instruct | 0.6839 / 0.6839 (identical outputs, also after `361a9a4c11`) | |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 | 0.3806 / 0.3806 | |
| Qwen3-4B + DFlash-b16 | 0.8613 / 0.8613 | 0.358 / 0.357 |
| MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B + DSpark | 0.5807 / 0.5807 (identical outputs) | 0.234 / 0.234 |
| Gemma4-E2B + MTP | 0.0614 / 0.0614 (identical outputs) | 0.645 / 0.645 |
| Qwen3-1.7B + Eagle3 | 0.6748, rerun 0.6740 / 0.6740 | 0.336 / 0.335 |

**E2/E3, bucketed reload and RL update.**
- E2 reloads the same checkpoint. E3 updates W0→W1 and compares bit-exactly with a cold W1 start in another process.
- Finish modes:
  - **layerwise:** `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`.
  - **plain:** `load_weights` + `process_weights_after_loading`, as verl does.
  - **api:** `reload_weights`.
- Call orders: one call, one tensor per call, and 512 MB buckets with each weight and its scale in different buckets, in both forward and reverse order.
- 18 models.
- No step fails only on the PR. Fixed by the PR (main fails, PR matches cold start bit-exactly):

| model | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3.2 4-layer slice | FP8 indexer `wk_weights_proj` differs after split loads | same as main (follow-up) |
| DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 slices | `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` on layerwise split loads | equal |
| Jina-v3 | LoRA-merge `KeyError` | same as main (follow-up) |
| Llama4 slice (DP vision) | `torch.cat` on `None` | equal |
| Molmo2-4B | missing `wte` halves | equal |
| Qwen3-4B DFlash, MiniCPM-V-4.7 DSpark drafters | meta-tensor crash or token mismatch on layerwise reloads | equal |
| Qwen3-4B DFlash drafter, default CUDA graphs (MRv2 FULL) | W0→W1 leaves the graph on the old fused KV: acceptance 0.014 vs 0.310 cold | acceptance equal to cold start on every step |
| Qwen3-1.7B | plain split load raises a false tied-alias error | equal |
| Phi-3-vision | every reload raises the tied-alias error | equal, W0→W1 included |

**E5/E6, real weight-transfer engines.**
- The engine tests pass identically on both arms:
  - `tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer*.py` (NCCL, UID, M2N): 207 passed, 23 skipped.
  - The RL weight-transfer entrypoint and worker tests: 33 passed.
- E6 runs real updates:
  1. `vllm serve --weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"nccl"}'` starts on W0.
  2. A trainer process broadcasts W1 from its safetensors (packed).
  3. It then sends W0 back.
  4. Greedy text and logprobs are compared with a cold W1 server and with the cold W0 outputs.

| model | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 (TP1, TP2), DeepSeek-V3.2 slice (TP1, TP2), MiMo-V2 slice, Llama4 slice, Qwen3-1.7B, MiniCPM-V-4.7 | equal | equal (Δlogprob 0.0) |
| Phi-3-vision | update raises the tied-alias error | equal |
| Molmo2-4B | update raises missing `wte` | equal |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 slice | `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` | equal |
| GLM5-next slice | stale `_merged_conv_weight` | same as main |

Known limitations: these fail on both arms and are not changed by this PR.
- **layerwise + a bucket buffer the sender reuses (zeroed after the call).** Layerwise staging keeps references to the caller's tensors without copying them, so any layer split across buckets is corrupted. All models hit this. With buffers that are not reused, the PR passes.
- **plain finish into already-processed FP8 params** (Qwen3-FP8, MiMo, GLM5-next, DSv3.2/V4/V4.1): the processed params can no longer take checkpoint tensors.
- **GLM5-next:** the KDA layer caches `_merged_conv_weight` on the first forward and never refreshes it. Any W0→W1 update leaves it stale, `reload_weights` and NCCL included. A separate fix will follow.
- **Gemma4 MTP drafter:** cannot be reloaded from the assistant checkpoint through `load_weights` (1536 vs 256 embed shape).
- **Hooks that cannot re-run:**
  - **dots3 vision MoE.** It FP8-packs the experts and then deletes the bf16 experts, so a vision reload has no target param and fails loudly.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 AMD MegaMoE.**
  - **XPU.**

**E4, unit tests:**
- The PR test set passes on the PR: `test_model_finalize.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_vl.py`, `test_lilicorr.py`, quark glm5next and `test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py`.
- Run on main, the new tests fail to import or fail.
- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/`, `tests/models/test_initialization.py` and the spec-decode set fail identically on both arms. The causes are offline HF hub, optional dependencies and gated models.
- `pre-commit` passes.

`test_model_finalize.py` covers:
- the reload finish runs the model hook exactly once;
- the Molmo/Molmo2 embedding halves split across calls, with a sub-range vocab shard;
- the BERT decoder tie.

`5abd76910` (stash removal, Molmo/Llama4 weight loaders) was rerun on GB200 with split and reordered delivery through layerwise reload: Molmo2-4B TP2 747/747 tensors byte-identical, Llama-4-Scout TP4 (`mm_encoder_tp_mode=data`, v → k → q) 1047/1047 byte-identical, identical greedy tokens; main fails both ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57733#issuecomment-6454258414)).

**Not validated at runtime:**
- XPU and ROCm: no hardware.
- Molmo v1: its remote code needs tensorflow, and startup fails on both arms. Molmo2 covers the shared code.

## Details

Verdicts over the 447 `load_weights`:

| verdict | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| per-weight | 364 | dispatch, remap or transform of the incoming tensor, routing, delegation |
| loader | 6 | model-loader entry points |
| moved | 19 | post-load work now in the hook |
| multi-part | 14 + 4 gated MTPs | Molmo/Molmo2 and Llama4 DP vision write each part through a weight loader; the rest keep main's handling (follow-up on #58382) |
| gated | 18 + 10 upstream | checks/decisions on this call's loaded set, complete loads only |
| exception | 14 | per-name choices that build no derived state (Roberta prefix sniff, Whisper zero `k_proj` bias, ColPali lazy head), Inkling EP padding, error paths |

Paths that do not run the hook are unchanged: kernel-format reload (`is_checkpoint_format=False`), sparse-NCCL patches and tensorizer. None of these call `load_weights`. The raw-tensorizer change is left to #55318. verl's FP8/QAT finish paths process layers themselves. Its default path calls `process_weights_after_loading(model, ...)` and gets the finish step.

**AI assistance.** Done with Claude Code.
- Codex, Kimi, Claude and Fable audited the diff and the coverage over several rounds.
- Confirmed findings were applied.
- The last rounds cut scope back to the split-load problem: tensorizer, the MiniCPM resampler move and the XPU forward change were reverted to main.

title: [Quantization] Keep deleted and renamed params registered after process_weights_after_loading
body:
## Overview

Part 3 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). After #62326 and #62405 (both merged), a loaded param can still disappear when PWAL deletes or renames it. This PR keeps those params registered, so after PWAL every loader-visible param is still registered under the same name, as the same object, and keeps its loaded data unless that would cost real memory.

## Claims

- **Renames alias one param under both names.** The new `move_parameter(layer, src, dst)` registers the `src` param object under `dst` as well and records `dst` as its runtime name. The loader writes through the checkpoint name and kernels read the runtime name, both pointing at one storage, so a later `replace_parameter` on either name updates both and no extra memory is used. This covers:
  - compressed-tensors `*_weight_packed` (linear, NVFP4/MXFP4/W4A8 MoE);
  - INC MXFP4;
  - the NVFP4 MoE oracle;
  - Humming NVFP4 and Humming's checkpoint-to-standard renames;
  - compressed-tensors W8A16 block FP8, which now aliases `weight_scale_inv` to `weight_scale`.
- **Loaded params no kernel reads keep their data and are marked retired** (`retire_parameter`). This covers:
  - consumed NVFP4 per-tensor scales (ModelOpt, Quark);
  - small Humming leftovers (at most 1/256 of the largest converted tensor);
  - the input scales of ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4 MoE when a weight-only backend (Marlin, Humming) is selected. These used to be set to `None`, which unregistered them. The method now leaves them registered and passes `None` to the MoE quant config.
- **Large released sources stay registered with empty storage** (`replace_parameter(layer, name, t.new_empty(0))`). Their data was converted into a different-layout kernel tensor, so keeping it would double that memory. This covers:
  - unused zero points, e.g. symmetric GPTQ `qzeros` (Conch, CPU, Marlin, Zentorch via `MPLinearKernel._release_unused_zp`; int8 scaled-mm; Quark int8 linear and MoE);
  - KV-cache scale placeholders (`kv_cache.py`, compressed-tensors KV);
  - released weights (XPU W4A8, wNa8o8, dynamic 4-bit, CPU int8, Triton MXFP4 MoE, INC ARK);
  - Humming leftovers larger than 1/256 of the largest converted tensor.
- **Not changed:** `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm` keeps `main`'s fresh `Parameter(empty(0))` on release, since the released weight can be a tied lm_head shared with `embed_tokens`.
- **Readers see the kernel view.**
  - `kernel_parameters(layer)` returns the live params, each object once under its runtime name. `get_live_param` treats retired or empty params as absent. Humming uses both helpers.
  - The Triton MXFP4 MoE wrapper is stored as a plain `<name>_triton` attribute read via `triton_weight()`, so it no longer takes over the param name.
- **Coverage** (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 73 delete/rename sites fixed here, plus 36 sites converted together with them (Humming's delete-then-recreate pattern), plus 7 n/a rows inside the changed hunks.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200 (rebased on `main`), the tests of every changed file: `tests/quantization/` (all), `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`, `model_loader/test_reload.py`, and the kernel/MoE/LoRA/model tests that import changed modules: 1609 passed.
  - Every remaining failure fails identically on `main` in the same image: Int8 cutlass on SM100, Hopper-only Machete/W4A8, gated repos, DeepGEMM UE8M0 `int32` scales on SM100 (`fp8_block_enabled[auto]`, `fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`), qutlass forward, int4 per-token KV kernel, AutoRound MXFP8 MoE `NotImplementedError`, and `test_kv_scale_reload`.
  - Existing tests that asserted a deleted or renamed param now assert it is still registered (renames alias the runtime name; Humming leaves the large unused checkpoint weights empty).
  - `test_keep_param_objects.py` runs ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 linear and MoE with Marlin and Humming forced; `test_utils.py` covers aliasing, retiring, and the runtime name.
- End-to-end on GB200 (before the rebase), `main` vs the stack with this PR. Each run is a cold start with GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot), greedy decoding, a byte digest of every post-PWAL tensor, and an object census of loader-visible params:

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors | Loader params registered (main → stack) | Kept with empty storage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ModelOpt NVFP4 (Qwen3-30B-A3B) | 0.8878 / 0.8886 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Marlin (3 runs each) | 0.8749, 0.8901, 0.8863 / 0.8779, 0.8893, 0.8855 | identical | 62% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Humming (3 runs each) | 0.8802, 0.8901, 0.8870 / 0.8734, 0.8863, 0.8961 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors NVFP4, forced Humming | 0.8931 / 0.8946 | identical | 36% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE (CUTLASS, `*_weight_packed` → `*_weight`) | 0.8582 / 0.8582 (1314/1319 identical text) | identical | 46% → 100% | 0 |

  - Marlin and Humming are not run-to-run deterministic. Two `main` runs agree on about 390 of 1319 GSM8K outputs, so their rows show three runs per arm.
  - The extra tensors in the stack are aliases, with no extra memory, or kept scalars and per-tensor scales. Kept data adds at most 0.15 MiB per model (under 0.001%).
- Direct load of W1 into the live params (`model.load_weights`, no PWAL): every checkpoint name now resolves.
  - On `main`, ModelOpt NVFP4 with Marlin or Humming fails with `has no parameter 'w2_input_scale'`, and compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE fails with `has no parameter 'w2_weight_packed'`.
  - With this stack, compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE loads all 675 tensors with no param moved. ModelOpt NVFP4 then stops at a shape mismatch, because Marlin/Humming repack to a different layout.
  - Direct load is only exact for layout-preserving PWAL, as on `main`; layerwise reload is the supported path.
- Layerwise reload W0 → W1:
  - ModelOpt NVFP4: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches `main` 8/8.
  - compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches 8/8.
- Earlier runs of the stack (#62326) gave `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 74 passed, 1 failed (`test_kv_scale_reload`), the same as on `main`.

## Details

- **Reload:** layerwise reload restores checkpoint-format params before loading. It goes through `layer._parameters`, so both alias names are restored, and a param kept empty is never handed to a `weight_loader`.
- **Humming:** used to delete every param and re-create the set it needs. It now writes through `replace_parameter`. Leftovers are skipped if they alias a replaced param, retired if small, and emptied if large.
- **Weight-only NVFP4 MoE input scales:** Humming's MoE quant config reads the input scales from the layer, so they are retired rather than left live. A live loaded scale would switch Humming to the static checkpoint scale, while `main` uses none.
- **Known limitation:** an aliased param appears under both names in `state_dict()`, so the UVA offloader and elastic-EP scale-up copy it twice (no data change).
- **Not kept (exceptions, listed in #62326):** the online FP8 requantization-source `weight_scale`, AutoGPTQ placeholder MoE biases, and torchao tensor subclasses.

---

## Update: loaded storage is never shrunk, emptied or split (0dcd74c070..682db58ae5)

A loader-visible param now keeps the checkpoint bytes it had at `create_weights` after PWAL. Its storage is never emptied. When two names refer to the same bytes, they are registered as one Parameter object. This supersedes the "kept with empty storage" item above for every site that has a plain tensor to back.

- **Shrink.** `replace_parameter` copies a smaller result into a prefix view of the param's own storage instead of rebinding it to a new, smaller allocation. Results of equal or larger size are still rebound. Online quantization (`uses_meta_device`) still frees its bf16 source. This covers:
  - ModelOpt/Quark NVFP4 MoE `w13_weight_scale_2` / `w13_input_scale` (`[E,2]` → `[E]`);
  - merged per-tensor scales (`[3]` → `[1]` or scalar: Humming NVFP4 `weight_scale_2`, CT NVFP4 `weight_global_scale` / `input_global_scale`, FP8 `input_scale.max()`);
  - the CUTLASS W4A8 FP8 scales and the CPU AWQ repack, which now go through `replace_parameter`.
- **Triton MXFP4 MoE.** The weights and scales are no longer emptied. Each param holds the swizzled storage, and its `triton_kernels` tensor points at it, so no second copy is kept.
- **Humming.** A converted tensor under a new name is registered as the leftover loaded param it came from (`move_parameter`). This applies when the tensor lives in that param's storage or replaces a large leftover; other leftovers are retired with their data.
  - This removes the second Parameter object that block-FP8 MoE `w13/w2_weight_scale` and NVFP4 `input_scale_2` had over `*_weight_scale_inv` / `input_global_scale`.
  - It also removes the emptied CT WNA16 `*_weight_packed`.
- **No more emptied loaded params.**
  - Unused zero points (Marlin, Conch, CPU, Zentorch), dynamic 4-bit scales and INC ARK qzeros/scales are retired with their data.
  - Zentorch, the DeepSeek-V4 CPU `wo_a` pack, CT W4A8 int8 MoE and CT WNA8O8 put the repacked tensor into the loaded param's storage. The K3 gfx942 MXFP4 repack no longer empties its source.
- **Not changed (reported):** sites whose kernel copy is opaque or split across several tensors still release the loaded weight. Keeping it would double weight memory:
  - CPU oneDNN int8 (`scaled_mm/cpu.py`) and `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`;
  - AMX MLA `kv_b_proj`;
  - the SM12x b12x linear/MoE/Q8_0 packs.
- **Coverage:** whole-tree AST call-graph enumeration from every PWAL root (1715 site rows), cross-checked with a `git grep` for release and alias patterns.
  - 1030 rows are not applicable: creation time, or not a loader param.
  - 409 `replace_parameter` rows are covered by the shrink rule.
  - The remaining rows were reviewed by hand. The `.data` rebinds there keep the same or a larger size, except the two converted above.

**Census on GB200** (verify-generic-restore census: C1 = storage ≥ checkpoint bytes, C2 = another param or buffer overlapping the bytes). Before = a693c5e9a2; after = 682db58ae5. 4-layer slices; gpt-oss-20b full.

| config | C1 before → after | C2 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE default / FI-CUTLASS / CuteDSL / vLLM CUTLASS | 8 → 0 each | 0 → 0 |
| ModelOpt NVFP4 Marlin / Humming | 4 / 8 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| CT NVFP4 default / Marlin | 8 → 0 | 12 → 12 (KV-scale buffer views, harmless) |
| CT NVFP4 Humming (new) | – → 0 | – → 12 (same KV-scale views) |
| gpt-oss Triton MXFP4 | 96 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Qwen3-30B block-FP8 Humming | 0 → 0 | 8 → 0 |

title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct weight reload: write checkpoint tensors into the live model
body:
> **Depends on #57733 and #62407 (merge those first); mypy/CI fail until they land.** This PR's diff is only the 8 direct-reload files. They import helpers that #57733 adds (`finalize_model_weights`, `discard_weight_parts`, `stash_weight_part`) and rely on #62407's kept parameter objects.
>
> Validated as the stack #57733 + #62407 + this PR + E1 (aoshen02/vllm#179) + derived-tensor in place (aoshen02/vllm#180), with same-weight direct reloads on GB200, NUPD=3. GSM8K is measured before and after, and every tensor is fingerprinted against cold start:
>
> | Model | Job | GSM8K pre → post | Tensors changed |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | DeepSeek-V4.1 | 40010 | 0.909 → 0.904 | 0/1709 |
> | MiniMax-M3.1 | 40013 | 0.951 → 0.951 | 0/3148 |
> | Muse Spark NVFP4 | 40042 | 0.839 → 0.838 | 0/3011 |
> | gpt-oss-120b TRTLLM MXFP4 (NUPD=2) | 39950 | 0.938 → 0.936 | 0/796 |

## Problem

RL weight sync reloads the checkpoint into a serving engine. The layerwise reload moves every layer to meta, materializes it again, loads the checkpoint and reruns post-load processing per layer. That costs a second copy of each layer at a time, and its correctness depends on per-layer completeness bookkeeping, so partial or reordered updates are hard to get right.

## Fix

`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` (registered in `vllm/envs.py`; the default stays `layerwise`) writes checkpoint tensors straight into the live model and reruns cold-start post-load processing once, at the startup addresses:

- At cold start, before `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL), record each tensor's checkpoint layout.
- `begin_direct_reload`, called from `initialize_layerwise_reload`, views every tensor whose layout PWAL changed back to its checkpoint layout, on the same storage. The loaders then write the checkpoint tensors in place.
- `finish_direct_reload`, called from `finalize_layerwise_reload`, clears the one-shot "already processed" guards and reruns PWAL for every module, then the model-level hook, as cold start does.
- `replace_parameter` keeps a parameter's address when PWAL changes its layout: under direct reload, the new tensor is written into a view of the existing storage when it fits.
- Refused at cold start: `draft_lm_head_quantization`. The quantized draft lm_head would be written into the target lm_head it shares.
- Refused at `begin`, before anything is modified:
  - no layout was recorded (also the case for pre-processed IPC weight-cache weights, already in runtime layout);
  - a storage is too small for its checkpoint layout.
- `sharded_rdt` refuses direct mode at init, because its replay plan is baked by a layerwise (meta) dry run.

**Delivery contract.** An update must deliver every checkpoint tensor of each module whose PWAL changes the tensor's layout or is not idempotent. Tensors without such processing, for example a frozen embedding table, may be left out and keep their bytes. **Nothing in this PR checks the contract**: until the completeness follow-up merges, a violation is not detected.

PWAL must keep every checkpoint tensor registered under its checkpoint name. This builds on #62407 (retire/alias instead of delete/rename).

**Known limitations.** Non-default MoE backends whose PWAL reallocates derived constants on a rerun are not yet refilled in place: TRTLLM FP8 per-tensor, FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/MXFP4, CuteDSL, and compressed-tensors FP8 constants. They are fixed in the derived-tensor follow-up. Online quantization is supported by a later follow-up.

## Tests

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py` uses a toy model with the hazards found on real models: a parent-derived tensor, a layout change, a loader bypass, a consumed scale and non-idempotent packing. It checks:
  - a reload equals a fresh cold start bit for bit, at unchanged addresses;
  - an unsent table without PWAL keeps its bytes;
  - refusals leave the model untouched;
  - an aborted update can be retried;
  - parked weight parts are handled.
- E2E (GB200, NCCL weight sync, 2 updates, reload diff on), this PR on #57733 + #62407 alone: Qwen3.8 GSM8K 0.971 → 0.970, 0/1434 tensors changed (39863); Nemotron 0.853 → 0.854, 0/913 changed (39864). For the full stack, see the table at the top.

## Dependencies / merge order

#57733 → #62407 → this PR. The follow-ups stack on this one: completeness check → moved-address/host-float check → side-tensor detector. The derived-tensor in-place PR, the NCCL `empty_cache` fix and the loader-bypass fix are independent.

title: [MoE] Zero expert padding on every load, not only at allocation
body:
## Problem

Some MoE backends round the expert intermediate (or hidden) size up. They allocate the padded parameters with zeros, and the loader writes only the part the checkpoint covers.

Post-load processing, however, reads the whole padded tensor. For example, TRT-LLM MXFP4 interleaves gate/up and shuffles rows over the padded size. On DeepSeek-V4.1 at TP4, the padding between w1 and w3 (rows 576..639 of each 640) ends up in the kernel layout.

A direct reload writes into storage that already holds post-processed weights, so that padding contains old kernel-layout bytes. Processing then copies them into the pad rows/columns of `w13_weight`, the w13/w2 scales and the gpt-oss biases, so the reloaded model no longer matches a cold start.

On DeepSeek-V4.1 (TP4, direct reload, two updates) this shows up as 120 tensors that differ from cold start: `w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` in every MoE layer.

## Fix

The loader now zeroes the padding it narrows away. It also zeroes the shard of a TP rank that receives no checkpoint rows. As a result, the checkpoint-layout tensor depends on the checkpoint alone. The grouped block-aligned TP path keeps its own unit-scale fill.

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py`:
  - padding is zeroed after a load into dirty storage;
  - the empty last-rank shard is zeroed;
  - block-aligned TP is unchanged.
- E2E, DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 direct reload: the reload diff drops from 120 to 0 of 1669 tensors.

## Dependencies / merge order

Stacks on #57733 (vllm-project/vllm#57733) and is needed by the direct-reload PR on DeepSeek-V4.1. Possible follow-up: zero each padded tensor in one pass instead of per expert (about 0.25 ms vs 30 ms per layer in a micro-benchmark).

title: [Model Loader] Write weight-derived tensors back in place on reload
body:
## Problem

`process_weights_after_loading` reruns on every weight reload (layerwise and direct). Many quant methods, kernels and models build tensors *derived* from the weights in that step: kernel constants, activation global scales, decode-path copies, fused drafter buffers. They allocate them as new tensors each time. Captured CUDA graphs and kernels keep reading the tensors from startup, so after a reload they read freed memory.

The weights themselves are reloaded correctly (diff 0 against cold start), yet accuracy drops or collapses. The symptom is model-specific and silent: no error, only wrong output.

## Fix

Write weight-derived tensors back into their startup storage on every rerun instead of allocating new ones.

- Parameters go through `replace_parameter`, which already refills in place; it now returns the kept parameter.
- Buffers and plain attributes go through the new `refill_derived(obj, name, tensor)`: copy in place when shape, dtype and device match, else replace. It returns the held tensor.
- MoE experts objects, which quant methods rebuild on every rerun, name their constants in `kept_constants`. `keep_constants(layer)` keeps them on the layer through `refill_derived` and hands them back to the new object.

Sites:

- **MoE kernel constants:**
  - TRTLLM MXFP4 SwiGLU `gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`.
  - TRTLLM FP8 `_g1_alphas/_g2_alphas/_g1_scale_c` and SwiGLU `gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`.
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS (FP8/NVFP4/MXFP4) SwiGLU constants and MXFP8 `fake_input_scale`.
  - CuteDSL NVFP4 `per_token_global_scale`.
  - FP8 per-tensor FlashInfer CUTLASS `g1/g2_alphas`.
  - NVFP4 MoE `a1/a2_gscale`.
  - TRTLLM NVFP4 `g1_scale_c` and `gemm1_*` (registered by the experts' post-load step; kept from the constructor for Quark NVFP4, which skips that step).
  - CUTLASS FP8 `ab/c_strides` and CUTLASS W4A8 `a/b/c/s_strides` (online `fp8_per_channel` MoE on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: illegal memory access after a reload before, GSM8K 0.644 → 0.623 with oracle unchanged after).
  - A runtime-dispatch wrapper (`FallbackExperts`: Triton-or-CUTLASS, Triton-or-DeepGEMM) passes `keep_constants` to both experts it holds.
- **Kimi-K3 specialized decode:** the packed MoE front, the padded TP16 dense down projection, and the KDA conv weight and FP32 norm. The MLA reciprocal q/k (inverse) scales are refilled in their buffers.
- **GLM-5-next:** indexer gate and KDA merged conv weight.
- **Drafters:**
  - DFlash/DSpark fused K/V and norm stacks (Qwen3, Laguna, Gemma4, Muse).
  - Gemma4 MTP gathered lm_head.
  - LiLiCorr inference buffers.
- **Muse Spark:**
  - The residual alpha/beta buffers.
  - The NVIDIA router output multiplier, now folded by the router weight's loader (once per load) instead of once per post-load run.
  - The NVIDIA NVFP4 MoE constants (`g1_alphas`, `g1_scale_c`, `g2_alphas`, `a1/a2_gscale`).

## Tests

Unit tests:

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: `refill_derived` refills buffers and attributes in place and never makes a parameter.
- `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py`: a rebuilt experts object keeps the first object's constant addresses, for TRTLLM MXFP4/FP8/NVFP4, FlashInfer CUTLASS, CuteDSL, CUTLASS FP8/W4A8 and a `FallbackExperts` wrapper. Also covers the FP8 FlashInfer CUTLASS scales.
- `tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py`: the router fold happens once per load; the NVFP4 MoE constants keep their addresses across reruns.

All pass on GB200 (slurm 39929, 40053, 40106).

E2E on GB200: same-weight NUPD≥2 reloads. GSM8K is compared before and after, and every tensor is fingerprinted against cold start.

**Reload in place (direct mode)**, stacked on #57733 + #62407 + #58382 (+ fork #179):

| Model | Job | GSM8K pre → post | Tensors changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark NVFP4 (NUPD=3) | 40042 | 0.8385 → 0.8378 (oracle PASS) | 0/3011 |
| Muse Spark NVFP4, this head (NUPD=3) | 40107 | 0.815 → 0.839 (oracle PASS; 98 lost / 130 gained of 1319, sampling noise) | 0/3311 |
| Muse Spark NVFP4, earlier head | 40090 | 0.836 → 0.823 (oracle PASS; 125 lost / 107 gained of 1319, within sampling noise) | 0/3311 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 (NUPD=3) | 40010 | 0.909 → 0.904 | 0/1709 |
| MiniMax-M3.1 vendor image (NUPD=3) | 40013 | 0.9507 → 0.9507 | 0/3148 |
| gpt-oss-120b TRTLLM MXFP4 | 39950 | 0.938 → 0.936 | 0/796 |

- **Muse before this PR:**
  - Without the router fold fix: 0.848 → 0.690, with 62 router weights differing from cold start (39889).
  - With the router fold fix but without the MoE constants fix: 0.833 → 0.751, with 420 tensors at new addresses (40036).
- **Address check:** with a moved-address check on, Muse 40044 completes NUPD=3 with nothing moved.

**Layerwise reload**, CuteDSL NVFP4 MoE, Qwen3-30B-A3B NVFP4:

| | Job | GSM8K pre → post |
|---|---|---|
| Base | 39882 | 0.832 → 0.039 |
| This PR | 39883 | 0.840 → 0.844 |

## Dependencies

Stacked on #62407 (keep param objects across post-load processing) and #57733 (post-load placement). The base branch of this PR is their merge, `5e23af126d`. Follow-up to #54477.

title: [Model] Inkling, Muse Spark: write checkpoint tensors through the parameter's weight loader
body:
## Problem

Weight reloads see only the writes that go through a parameter's (wrapped) `weight_loader`; for example, layerwise reload loads into meta-device parameters through it. Two models write around it:

- **Inkling** copies its routed and sink expert tensors straight into the parameters, because the checkpoint layout needs de-interleaving and per-expert slot writes. As a result, a reload leaves every expert at its startup values.
- **Muse Spark's fused QKV+O-gate linear** calls `self.weight_loader` directly, and v2-loader linear methods bind `weight_loader_v2` to its parameters. Both bypass the parameter's loader.

## Fix

- **Inkling:** the expert parameters get a weight loader that runs the given write, and every expert write goes through it. The nvidia and amd backends share these loaders in `inkling/common/weights.py`.
- **Muse Spark:** `weight_loader_v2` is routed to the layer's loader, and `load_weights` loads through `param.weight_loader`.

## Tests

There is no new unit test: the change only routes existing writes through the loader. These two models have not had a reload E2E run on this branch yet (that is the next step).

## Dependencies

None.

title: [Perf][FlashAttention] FA4: pass no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

For an FP8 KV cache whose per-tensor scales are 1.0, FlashAttention now passes FA4 no descale at all. Before, it passed broadcast descale views that FA4 copied into contiguous tensors, three copy kernels per attention layer and step.

This PR began as the squash of the whole MiniMax-M3.1-Flash tree. That squash has since been split into the PRs below; this PR now holds only the FA4 change.

## How #63232 was split

| Part of the original squash | Where it went | State |
|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3.1 model and DSpark draft model, with their kernels (MSA NVFP4 KV cache and indexer, MegaMoE staging, ROCm MXFP8 linears, ...) | #64111 | merged |
| ROCm: NVFP4 MoE re-quantization to MXFP4/MXFP8, and fused shared experts through online quantization | #64378 | merged |
| FA4: no FP8 descale for a unit per-tensor scale | this PR | open |
| NIXL P/D: re-sharding NVFP4 KV pages across heterogeneous TP (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | #64475 | open |
| Scheduler: keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups | #64472 | open |
| DSpark/DFlash draft step: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, wider DFlash padding, `is_padding` from the positions kernel, top-p fix | #64476 | open |
| Batch-sharded DSpark draft sampling | dropped from #64476; #63886 covers it | open (#63886) |
| SimpleCPUOffload: one host buffer per rank with HugeTLB pages | already open as #60130; the squash's extra ROCm change (SDMA copy-engine flag for batched copies) was pushed onto #60130 | open (#60130) |
| Scheduler draft-slot change | dropped: `main`'s `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting` already returns 0 for DFlash/DSpark | – |
| Sparse paged-attention KV block count fix (ROCm) | dropped: already on `main` via #63270 | – |

The full squash as it was before the split is a0ea941097 (on 5d35ce3934), in this PR's force-push history.

PRs that were opened against this branch (`minimax-m31-flash`) while it held the squash: #64359, #64273, #64264, #64206, #63528, #63491 and #62509. Their diffs against this branch now include the whole old squash (e.g. #64359 shows 193 files). The model (#64111) and the ROCm re-quantization (#64378) are on `main`, so they can retarget `main`.

## Claims

- **Unit scales:** when FA4 runs with a per-tensor Q/K/V scale of exactly 1.0, `FlashAttentionImpl` passes `None` for that descale.
  - FA4 reads a missing descale as 1.0, so the output is bit-identical.
  - FA4's `maybe_contiguous` no longer copies the three broadcast descale views per layer and step.
- **Other scales:** calibrated per-tensor scales and per-head scales keep their descale tensors. Other FlashAttention versions get the same broadcast descale as before; only the strides of its size-1 dims are made canonical, which changes metadata, not values.
- **(1, 1) descale views:** a view with one sequence and one KV head per rank now gets canonical strides. FA4 treats such a view as contiguous and skips its copy, and its layout check then rejects the zero stride.

## Validation

On GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
```

148 passed, 9 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 failures are `test_sliding_window_encoder_backend_correctness` (embeddinggemma-300m). They fail the same way on `main` (2abde627d9) in this environment.

The new `test_flash_attn_fa4_unit_fp8_descale_is_exact` (Blackwell only) checks that:

- a unit scale gives no descale;
- FA4's output with no descale equals its output with the broadcast unit descale, bit for bit;
- a descale of 2 changes the output, so the comparison is not vacuous;
- calibrated and per-head scales keep their descale tensors.

Not covered:

- No end-to-end benchmark on this branch; the three copy kernels saved per layer and step were not timed.
- No accuracy eval: the output is bit-identical by the test above.
- The (1, 1) stride case is not in the new test, which uses 3 sequences and 4 KV heads.

## Details

- **Why the check is on the host:** the scales are fixed once the weights are loaded, so the `_scale_float` mirrors decide the case on the host with no GPU sync. A per-head scale's float mirror holds only its maximum, so the check also requires a single-element scale.
- **Compiled kernels:** FA4 compiles a separate kernel without descales, since descale presence is part of its compile key. A model with unit scales always takes that kernel.
- **Not a duplicate:** the open FA4 PRs change other things. #48156 warms up the paged FA4 kernels, #60372 adds SM90 FP8 MMA for Gemma-4, #63328 is sparse-MLA FP8 prefill, and #54705 covers Inkling per-tensor scales outside `flash_attn.py`. None of them changes how `FlashAttentionImpl` passes descales.

Credits: qizixi wrote the FA4 change and is a co-author in the commit. AI assistance (Claude) was used to split the original squash into the PRs above, to write the FA4 test and to draft this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests above.
